hook.line: The café has to close for a day, and nobody wanted that. Spanish has short ways to say there is no choice, with a shrug built in.
hook.es: No queda de otra que cerrar hoy.
hook.en: There's no choice but to close today.

examples.es: No hay más remedio que esperar hasta mañana.
examples.en: There's nothing for it but to wait until tomorrow.

examples.es: No queda de otra que pagar.
examples.en: There's no option but to pay.
We have no choice but to get up early.

examples.es: No queda de otra que vender el café.
examples.en: There's no choice but to sell the café.

examples.es: ¿No hay más remedio que cerrar todo el día?
examples.en: Is there really no choice but to close all day?

examples.es: Toca esperar la respuesta de Altamira.
examples.en: We just have to wait for Altamira's answer.

rule:
All three frames say the same thing: you have no choice, so you do it. English says "there's nothing for it but to..." or "I guess we have to...". Spanish keeps a fixed frame and then a plain infinitive:
*No hay más remedio que* + infinitive
*No queda de otra que* + infinitive (everyday in Latin America)
*Toca* + infinitive (short and very Colombian)
Nobody is named, so the same sentence works for *I*, *we* or anyone. The mood is a shrug, not anger.
smallPrint: Teachers call these impersonal expressions of necessity. Here *tocar* means that something falls to you to do.

readAndPick.es: No queda de otra que pagar.
options: We can pay another time.
There's no option but to pay.
Nobody else is going to pay.
We have no choice but to get up early.
It's too early to get up.
We got up early.

readAndPick.es: No hay más remedio que esperar hasta mañana.
options: There's no more waiting until tomorrow.
I'd rather wait until tomorrow.
There's nothing for it but to wait until tomorrow.

readAndPick.es: No queda de otra que vender el café.
options: We'd rather sell the café.
There's no choice but to sell the café.
Nobody is left to sell the café.

readAndPick.es: Toca esperar la respuesta de Altamira.
options: Altamira is waiting for our answer.
Altamira has already answered.
We just have to wait for Altamira's answer.

readAndPick.es: ¿No hay más remedio que cerrar todo el día?
options: Is there really no choice but to close all day?
Did we close all day?
Why is it closed all day?

readAndPick.es: No hubo más remedio que cerrar.
options: I want to close.
I didn't close.
There was no choice but to close.

readAndPick.es: No hay más remedio que llamar a Vale.
options: Vale has to call us.
There's no way around it: we have to call Vale.
We shouldn't call Vale.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *que* or *de*, then type the whole sentence: No hay más remedio ___ esperar hasta mañana. (There's nothing for it but to wait until tomorrow.)
yourTurn.answer: No hay más remedio que esperar hasta mañana.
yourTurn.why: The frame always closes with *que* before the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *esperar* or *espero*, then type the whole sentence: Toca ___ la respuesta de Altamira. (We just have to wait for Altamira's answer.)
yourTurn.answer: Toca esperar la respuesta de Altamira.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: There's no choice but to sell the café.
yourTurn.answer: No queda de otra que vender el café.
accept: No hay más remedio que vender el café.
yourTurn.why: Both frames are everyday; each is followed by the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: There's nothing for it but to wait until tomorrow.
yourTurn.answer: No hay más remedio que esperar hasta mañana.
accept: No queda de otra que esperar hasta mañana.
yourTurn.why: The frame plus *esperar* says it all.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: We have no choice but to get up early.
accept: No queda de otra que madrugar.
No hay más remedio que madrugar.
yourTurn.why: *Toca* is the shortest of the three frames.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a question: *No hay más remedio que cerrar todo el día.* becomes: Is there really no choice but to close all day?
yourTurn.answer: ¿No hay más remedio que cerrar todo el día?
yourTurn.why: Keep the same words and add the question marks.

yourTurn.prompt: Put it in the past: *No hay más remedio que cerrar.* becomes: There was no choice but to close.
yourTurn.answer: No hubo más remedio que cerrar.
yourTurn.why: Only *hay* changes: in the past it becomes *hubo*.

pitfalls.wrong: No hay más remedio de esperar.
pitfalls.right: No hay más remedio que esperar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The frame closes with *que*, not *de*.
Almost. *Toca* is followed straight by the infinitive, with no *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: No hay más remedio que esperamos.
pitfalls.right: No hay más remedio que esperar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Nobody is named in this frame, so the verb stays as a plain infinitive.

personal: Tell me about something you did recently because there was no choice. Use *toca* or *no queda de otra que*.
